newsitem.title: USA: Helsinki Commission calls for calm in Albania poll.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki Commission calls for calm in Albania poll.

text.p: The U.S. Commission on Security and Cooperation in Europe on Wednesday appealed for calm in Sunday's general election in Albania and urged the world community to provide continuing support.

The statement, issued by commission co-chairmen Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, and Representative Christopher Smith, a New Jersey Republican, also called upon all parties involved in the elections to respect the poll's results.

"We call upon all citizens of Albania to refrain from violence on election day, to participate in the elections, and to cooperate with election officials, international election observers and peacekeeping forces," they said.
Other countries in the international community should "provide continuing support as Albania takes this next step out of its crisis," the statement continued.

Events in Albania over the past seven years reflected "the Albanian people's strong desire for human rights, democracy, free enterprise, and the benefits of integration into Europe and participation in world affairs," D'Amato and Smith said.
"We are counting on that strong desire to move Albania forward again," the statement added.
The commission was formed in 1976 to monitor the Helsinki Accords. It is comprised of nine senators, nine representatives, and one official each from the state, commerce and defence departments.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in Albania, Europe's poorest country, since the beginning of the year in unrest that began with popular anger over the collapse of shady savings schemes.
About 50 people have died in the past week alone as the campaign for Sunday's general election draws to a close.

The elections were called to form a new government with enough popular support to lead Albania out of a crisis triggered by fraudulent pyramid schemes in which most Albanians invested, often costing them their life savings.
